transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

I'm here because I've been feeling extremely anxious and distressed lately. I am convinced that I am being watched and constantly monitored by other people, and this has been going on for about two months now.
Besides feeling like you are being watched, have you heard any voices or seen things that other people don't seem to hear or see?

Yes, I actually have. I keep hearing these quiet whispers and voices talking about me when I'm alone, and it's really distressing. Sometimes I also see dark, shadowy figures out of the corner of my eye that aren't actually there.
Along with these experiences, have you noticed any major changes in your mood, like feeling very down and depressed, or feeling unusually energetic and active?
No, I haven't really noticed feeling unusually down or overly energetic. My mood has been pretty much the same, just very anxious because of the monitoring.

latest_inference.note: Previously, the candidates were Schizophrenia, Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type), Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type), Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features, and Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features. Since the patient denies experiencing any major mood episodes (neither depressive nor manic/hypomanic), we can rule out Schizoaffective Disorder (both Bipolar and Depressive types), Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features, and Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features. This narrows the diagnosis down to Schizophrenia.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with prominent persecutory delusions (feeling watched and monitored) and sensory hallucinations (hearing whispers and seeing shadowy figures) for approximately two months. The absence of significant mood disturbances (depressive or manic episodes) rules out mood disorders with psychotic features and schizoaffective disorder, making Schizophrenia the most appropriate diagnosis from the allowed candidates.
